'''Michael A. Levi''' is a policy expert who served as Special Assistant to the President for Energy and Economic Policy in the [[Presidency of Barack Obama|Obama White House]] from 2016 to 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wolff |first=Eric |date=2016-07-19 |title=GOP platform proposes turning EPA into a commission |url=https://www.politico.com/tipsheets/morning-energy/2016/07/gop-platform-proposes-turning-epa-into-a-commission-215402 |access-date=2017-05-25 |website=POLITICO}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Restuccia |first=Andrew |date=2016-07-18 |title=Michael Levi joining White House as energy adviser |url=https://subscriber.politicopro.com/article/2016/07/michael-levi-joining-white-house-energy-adviser-074875 |access-date=2025-05-07 |website=POLITICO Pro |language=en}}</ref> He was previously the David M. Rubenstein senior fellow for energy and environment at the [[Council on Foreign Relations]] (CFR), a nonpartisan foreign-policy [[think tank]] and membership organization, and director of its Maurice R. Greenberg Center for Geoeconomic Studies. He is an expert on energy and climate, highly regulated technology, and defense and security policy.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.cfr.org/experts/energy-climate-oil-security/michael-a-levi/b11890| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120218130822/http://www.cfr.org/experts/energy-climate-oil-security/michael-a-levi/b11890| archive-date = 2012-02-18| title = Michael A. Levi - Council on Foreign Relations}}</ref>

==Education==
Levi holds a BSc (Hons.) in mathematical physics from [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]], and an MA degree in physics from [[Princeton University]], where he studied [[string theory]] and cosmology. He also holds a PhD in war studies from [[King's College London]] where he was the SSHRC William E. Taylor fellow.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2014-03-26 |title=Michael A. Levi |url=https://docs.house.gov/meetings/FA/FA00/20140326/101956/HHRG-113-FA00-Bio-LeviM-20140326.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170217125351/https://docs.house.gov/meetings/FA/FA00/20140326/101956/HHRG-113-FA00-Bio-LeviM-20140326.pdf |archive-date=2017-02-17 |access-date=2025-05-07 |website=U.S. House of Representatives Document Repository}}</ref>

==Career==
Levi was previously a fellow for science and technology at the Council and, before that, a nonresident science fellow and a science-and-technology fellow in foreign policy studies at the [[Brookings Institution]]. He was previously director of the flagship Strategic Security Project of the [[Federation of American Scientists]].<ref name=":0" />

==Books==
Dr. Levi is author of ''The Power Surge: Energy, Opportunity, and the Battle for America’s Future'' ([[Oxford University Press]], May 2013 {{ISBN|978-0199986163}}).<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.cfr.org/energy/power-surge/p29746| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130104101147/http://www.cfr.org/energy/power-surge/p29746| archive-date = 2013-01-04| title = The Power Surge - Council on Foreign Relations}}</ref> In ''The Power Surge'', Levi details two unfolding energy revolutions in the United States, and the implications that they might have for America's economy, national security, and environment. Levi uses historical analysis, scientific data, and on-the-ground reporting to establish that America's energy future need not be a [[zero-sum game]].<ref>{{cite news|title=America's Energy Future: Meet the Frackers|newspaper=The Economist|date=15 June 2013|url=https://www.economist.com/news/books-and-arts/21579431-making-sense-americas-new-energy-resources-meet-frackers|accessdate=16 July 2013}}</ref>  He argues that the best path forward lies in a strategy that increases "opportunities for energy production of all kinds, while penalizing dangerous energy consumption that would worsen climate change and sustain U.S. dependence on oil."<ref>{{cite journal|last=Levi|first=Michael|title=America's Energy Opportunity: How to Harness the New Sources of U.S. Power|journal=Foreign Affairs|date=May–June 2013|volume=92|issue=3|url=http://www.foreignaffairs.com/articles/139111/michael-levi/americas-energy-opportunity?page=show|accessdate=16 July 2013}}</ref>

Levi is also the author of the book ''[[On Nuclear Terrorism]]'' ([[Harvard University Press]], 2007)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hup.harvard.edu/catalog.php?isbn=9780674032385|title=On Nuclear Terrorism — Michael Levi}}</ref> and coauthor with [[Michael E. O'Hanlon]] of ''The Future of Arms Control'' (Brookings Institution Press, 2005).<ref>{{cite book |isbn=978-0815764632 |title=The Future of Arms Control |last1=Levi |first1=Michael A. |last2=O'Hanlon |first2=Michael E. |date=2005 |publisher=Brookings Institution Press }}</ref> His 2005 monograph with Michael D’Arcy, ''Untapped Potential: U.S. Science and Technology Cooperation with the Islamic World'' was the first comprehensive study of science and technology in the [[Muslim world]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.brookings.edu/research/papers/2005/04/islamicworld-levi|title=Untapped Potential: US Science and Technology Cooperation with the Islamic World|date=30 November 2001}}</ref>  His recent writings include studies of natural gas exports, the Canadian [[oil sands]], and the global politics and economics of clean energy innovation.<ref>{{cite news| url = http://www.foreignaffairs.com/author/michael-levi| title = Michael Levi {{!}} Foreign Affairs| newspaper = Foreign Affairs| date = 28 January 2009}}</ref>

==Other==
Levi has been invited to testify before Congress where he presented expert scientific evidence to the National Academy of Sciences. Levi was project director for the CFR-sponsored Independent Task Force on climate change, co-chaired by former governors Tom Vilsack and George Pataki. He participated in the 2010 Hertog Global Strategy Initiative, a high-level research program on [[nuclear proliferation]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://globalstrategy.columbia.edu/summer2010/ |title=Summer 2010 « Hertog Global Strategy Initiative at Columbia University |accessdate=2013-03-08 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121220210604/http://globalstrategy.columbia.edu/summer2010/ |archivedate=2012-12-20 }}</ref> His essays have been published in ''Foreign Affairs'', ''[[Foreign Policy]]'', ''Nature'', ''Scientific American'', among others. His op-eds have appeared in ''The New York Times'', ''The Washington Post'', ''The Wall Street Journal'', and ''Financial Times''. Dr. Levi previously wrote a monthly online column on science and security for the ''New Republic'', and served as a technical consultant to the critically acclaimed television drama ''24''. He currently writes a blog on energy, climate, and nuclear issues.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.cfr.org/experts/energy-climate-oil-security/michael-a-levi/b11890/blog| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120729231114/http://www.cfr.org/experts/energy-climate-oil-security/michael-a-levi/b11890/blog| archive-date = 2012-07-29| title = Michael A. Levi - Council on Foreign Relations}}</ref>
